title: 碑亭 Bei ting
subtitle: Yuanming Yuan

model.line: The library of the Four Treasuries in its walled rock garden, as S01 draws the court and the texts and the dig of 2024 describe it: the library's six bays and its depth from the Guangxu 丈尺册 (B), two storeys outside with the skirt roof of its sisters 文津阁 and 文渊阁, black glazed tile with green trim (the dig), the terrace on the pool, 玲峰 on its stone terrace in the water, the stele pavilion, the rockeries, the wall and the gates; every height and the smaller buildings' forms are C. No picture of 文源阁 standing is known.
rows: 文源阁 (1774; S05 上下各六楹): six bays from the west, the stair bay 1.60 m, 4.00, 4.00, the 明间 5.12, 4.00, 4.00 m, 22.72 m, and 14.72 m deep with galleries of 3.52 m front and back (the Guangxu 丈尺册, S105: B; S01 draws the same grid within 1-1.6 m); doors in the 明间, windows in the other bays, the stair bay at the west

Two storeys outside, three inside (S105: a mezzanine), a skirt roof 腰檐 front and back between grey brick gable walls (S105; the form of 文津阁, which the 1776 poem says it copies, and of 文渊阁: twins, form only); dark green columns (S105), red frames (the sisters); the plaque 文源閣 in Qianlong's hand under the upper eave (S05); the storeys measured on 文渊阁's front (P0555) in 文源阁's bays: columns 2.51 m, the skirt's drip 3.34 m, the upper windows 5.08-6.15 m, the top eave's drip 7.26 m above the floor (a twin's proportion, C; Q287)

硬山 in black glazed tile with green trim (the dig, S133; S105), the ridges green with white waves (Malone saw fragments of white-and-green wave-pattern tile, S02 p.90); a 歇山 is also argued for (Q111): 硬山 follows 文津阁 and 天一阁

The pool before the library (S01; Round 10's water) with rock banks (Malone) and the terrace 月台 on its north side (S01; the 1776 poem's 月臺); 玲峰 on its oval stone terrace in the water (S01; the dig: a base of long slabs tied with iron dovetails), 4.1 m high (Malone's '12 or 15 feet': B; S105 says over 6 m, Q288), pierced, Qianlong's poem cut on it (S05); its form C
East of the library (S05: 閣東亭内石碣刋御製文源閣記): its platform 4.48 m square (the 丈尺册, S105; Q110), the stele of the 文源阁记 (Malone saw it standing); the pavilion's form and tile C

Rock banks inside the wall, rock masses in the corners and the rockery between the pool and the south gate as S01 draws them (the 1776 poem: 詭石堆竒岫; the dig: culverts under the rockery behind the gate); 趣亭 on its summit (named by the dig, S133; its place and form C, after the sister's pavilion on its rockery, P0550); a small pond in the north-east corner (the dig, S942; place and size C)

The court's wall of 虎皮石 rubble (the dig, S133), the three-bay south gate and the north gate (S01; the dig); their heights and forms C; the court raised a little above the land outside (the dig, S942; its level C)

The library and the stele pavilion's platforms, the gate and its steps, the base of 玲峰 and its broken pieces (S105, S134; dug in 2024 by 北京市考古研究院, S133); Malone saw the marble stele still standing in the 1930s (S02 p.89); where it stands now is not in what we have read

Every height (the storeys after the sister 文渊阁, the platform 0.75 m, the court 0.1 m, the roof's rise), the end piers and corbels, the rails, the wave crests' form, the gates', the stele pavilion's and 趣亭's forms, the rocks' shapes and heights, the pond's place: the classes, the Qing manual and the sisters' photographs (C, the pale tint with conf=1)

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 文源阁
evidence.excerpt_zh: 水木明瑟之北稍西為文源閣上下各六楹閣西為栁浪聞鶯（圓明園册）臣等謹按文源閣乾隆三十九年建與文華殿後之文淵閣避暑山莊之文津閣皆以貯四庫全書閣額及閣内汲古觀瀾額皆御書聨曰因溯委以會心是處原泉來活水即登髙而遊目當前奥㝔對玲峯屏扆聨曰寧誇池館消閒暇雅喜詩書悅性靈檐柱聨曰討尋宜富波瀾浩矣無涯神智益披攬直探星宿挹之不盡古今涵亦御書閣前石為玲峯刋御製文源閣詩閣東亭内石碣刋御製文源閣記恭錄卷内
evidence.summary: 文源閣, six bays on each floor, built 乾隆三十九年 (1774) as one of the Four Treasuries libraries, beside 文淵閣 and 文津閣; 栁浪聞鶯 to the west. The note gives its couplets and the 玲峯 rock before it, with a poem cut on the rock and the 文源閣記 on a stele in the east pavilion.

evidence.title: 文源阁 Wenyuan Ge, library of the Four Treasuries
evidence.excerpt_other: The central point of interest in this rock garden was in the huge monolith with inscriptions on it and pierced with many holes, rising 12 or 15 feet from a stone terrace in the middle of the pool.
evidence.summary: Copied by measurement from the Fan family library in Zhejiang (天一阁), per Qianlong's account carved on a marble stele of 1774, still standing when Malone wrote. Glazed tiles with a wave design in white and green, fragments still on site; a pool before the library, water-worn rock round it, and the inscribed monolith 玲峰 rising 12 or 15 ft from a stone terrace in the pool.

evidence.title: 杨菁 等, 圆明园文源阁, 圆明园研究 63
evidence.summary: Group about 16,000 m2, building about 700 m2, modelled on 天一阁. Library six bays by five, galleries front and rear, 硬山, black glazed tile with green edging, grey brick walls and dark green columns. A lower floor with study and west stair, mezzanine and a top floor of shelves. 玲峰 over 6 m high. Based on Yangshi Lei plans including one of 1894.

evidence.title: 杨菁, 杨文艳, 牛颖倩, 殷双 (天津大学建筑学院), 圆明园文源阁, 圆明园研究 63: survey of the ruin and the Guangxu 丈尺册
evidence.summary: The authors measured and scanned the cleared ruin before the 2024 dig: the library and stele pavilion platforms are fairly whole, the gate, steps and the cracked-ice floor can be seen, the square pond has gone, and black glazed and green glazed fragments lie about. The verbatim line is the Guangxu-reign 丈尺册 (a Qing text, quoted by the authors) giving the six bays and the depth. Their measured area is the smallest of the four northern libraries, close to 文津阁.

evidence.title: 文源阁 public day and results, 新华网, 北京晚报 via visitbeijing, 总台 via 凤凰网
evidence.summary: From 2024-08-26, 1,000 m2 planned. Site was the 四达亭 pavilion under Yongzheng, rebuilt 1775. Water system: one supply culvert under the north wall, four drains and a 沟门 outlet in the south wall, ground inside higher than outside. 玲峰 stone base of long slabs tied with iron dovetails. Original surface about 0.5 m down, with irregular stone paths and Y-forks not shown on any plan. Glazed fittings and porcelain sherds.

evidence.title: 文源阁 2024 dig, 人民日报海外版 via 新华网
evidence.summary: Aug to Nov 2024: gate, stele pavilion, terrace, 趣亭, north gate, walls, roads and waterways. Dig confirms six bays and black glazed roof tiles. Two ponds, one in front and one east of the library; walls of 虎皮石 rubble, not city brick; stele pavilion founded on cedar pegs, stone slabs and rammed 三合土. Five stone culverts run under the walls, three of them under the rockery behind the gate.

evidence.title: Old Summer Palace findings reveal fresh details of complex planning (文源阁 dig 2024)
evidence.summary: The 文源阁 court was a closed yard with a door south and north, holding the main hall, two pavilions and a viewing terrace linked by paths of unworked flagstones. Two ponds, one in the north-east corner and one south of the hall, were tied by channels to the river outside for fire water, and the yard was raised a little so storm water left through a wall drain. Foundations were trench, timber piles, stone slabs, then the base, the soundest found so far in the gardens; the layout matches Yangshi Lei sketches of 1779 and 1898.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
